extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and parties in TTAB (Trademark Trial and Appeal Board) inter partes proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for serving, responding to, and objecting to interrogatories and requests for production in TTAB trademark proceedings, including counting rules, timing, form/content of responses, and ESI considerations. Covers procedural remedies (motions to compel), signatures/authority, and practical expectations for handling voluminous or foreign-held information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting interrogatories and subparts
rubrics_metrics.description: If an interrogatory requests information concerning more than one issue (e.g., both “sales and advertising figures,” or both “adoption and use”), the Board will count each issue on which information is sought as a separate interrogatory. In contrast, if an interrogatory requests “all relevant facts and circumstances” concerning a single issue, event, or matter; or asks that a particular piece of information be given for multiple years and/or for each of the responding party's involved marks, it will be counted as a single interrogatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble/instructions are not counted as interrogatories or subparts. Parties should be mindful of 37 CFR § 2.120(d)(1) numerical limits and count issues rather than literal sentence breaks. Recommended to set out counting method when dispute arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductory instructions/preamble not binding on adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The introductory instructions or preamble to a set of interrogatories will not be counted by the Board as interrogatories or subparts for purposes of numerical limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the Board's determination on the adequacy of an interrogatory answer will not be governed by the preamble; the Board is not bound by the instructions or preamble and will independently determine adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for excessive interrogatories — general objection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party believes the number of interrogatories served exceeds the limitation in 37 CFR § 2.120(d)(1) and will not waive objection, the party shall, within the time for (and instead of) serving answers and specific objections, serve a general objection on the ground of excessive number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party should not answer the first 75 interrogatories and object to the rest as excessive. Serving a general objection in lieu of answers preserves the objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to compel following general objection — contents and conferral
rubrics_metrics.description: If the propounding party files a motion to compel discovery in response to a general objection, the motion must be accompanied by a copy of the set(s) of interrogatories said to exceed the limitation and must comply with 37 CFR § 2.120(e) requirements, including a written statement that the moving party has made a good faith effort to resolve issues by conference or correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended the moving party set out its counting method showing the number of interrogatories does not exceed 75. See TBMP § 523 for motions to compel guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board's remedy when interrogatories found excessive
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board finds the interrogatories are excessive and the propounding party has not used up its allotted interrogatories, the Board normally will allow the propounding party an opportunity to serve a revised set of interrogatories not exceeding the numerical limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revised set serves as a substitute and is deemed timely if the excessive set was timely. If a revised set is served after the close of discovery, it may not seek information beyond the scope of the excessive set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to respond to document requests due to excessive interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Although there are no numerical limitations on document requests, a party may refuse to respond to a document request seeking all documents identified or referred to in response to interrogatories if the number of interrogatories is believed to be excessive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law supports refusal where answering interrogatories is prerequisite to producing documents and interrogatories are excessive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to respond to interrogatories and production requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses to interrogatories, requests for production of documents and things, and requests for admission must be served within thirty (30) days from the date of service of such discovery requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service is by first-class mail, Express Mail, or overnight courier, date of mailing/delivery is service date and five extra days are allowed. No extra time for agreed electronic service (e.g., fax or e-mail). See 37 CFR § 2.119(c) and TBMP § 403.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to respond timely
rubrics_metrics.description: A party that fails to respond within the allowed time, and cannot show excusable neglect, may be found on motion to compel to have forfeited its right to object to the discovery requests on their merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merits objections include claims of irrelevance, over-breadth, vagueness, burden/oppression, or lack of likely admissible evidence. Privilege/confidentiality/work-product objections are not merits objections and are treated differently. Courts have discretion; parties should attempt to determine why no response was made before moving to compel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of interrogatory responses — separate, full, under oath
rubrics_metrics.description: Each interrogatory must, to the extent it is not objected to, be answered separately and fully in writing under oath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responding party should reproduce each interrogatory immediately preceding its answer or objection (Board preference). If answered, the answer must be made separately and fully in writing under oath; if objected, reasons must be stated in lieu of an answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of grounds for objections
rubrics_metrics.description: The grounds for objecting to an interrogatory must be stated with specificity; any ground not stated in a timely objection is waived unless excused for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections going to the merits must be preserved timely or may be forfeited. Confidentiality objections are expected to be extremely limited because a standard protective order is in place for Board inter partes proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to answer by specifying business records (Fed. R. Civ. P. 33(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an interrogatory’s answer may be determined by examining, auditing, compiling, abstracting, or summarizing business records and the burden of deriving the answer is substantially the same for either party, the responding party may answer by specifying the records to be reviewed and providing a reasonable opportunity to examine and audit them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification must be in sufficient detail to enable the interrogating party to locate and identify the records as readily as the responding party could. The responding party may instead include the information itself in its written answer. If invoking Rule 33(d) for ESI, technical support or assistance may be required to afford adequate opportunity to derive the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations when invoking business-records option for ESI
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking to invoke Fed. R. Civ. P. 33(d) with regard to electronic information may be required to provide technical support, information on application software, or other assistance to the requesting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If direct access to the answering party's electronic information system is necessary, privacy/confidentiality concerns may justify deriving/ascertaining the answer internally rather than providing access. Producing records in a foreign language without translation may be insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privilege and business-records option incompatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A responding party cannot simultaneously invoke the option to produce business records and claim the protection of a privilege as to the documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documents are privileged, the party cannot avoid answering by pointing to privileged records; privilege must be asserted and justified separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to interrogatories — motions attacking interrogatories generally inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: It is generally inappropriate for a party to respond to interrogatories by filing a motion attacking them (e.g., motion to strike, suppress, protective order); the party ordinarily should answer proper interrogatories and state objections to improper ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of motions to attack interrogatories is discouraged; TBMP § 410 addresses such practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to supplement discovery responses
rubrics_metrics.description: A party has a duty to supplement responses to interrogatories as set forth in TBMP § 408.03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should monitor for new, changed, or corrected information and timely supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and authority for interrogatory responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatories must be answered by the party served or, if the party is a corporation/partnership/association/governmental agency, by an officer, partner, or agent who must furnish the information available to the party. The person who makes the answers must sign them, and the attorney who objects must sign any objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'agent' includes an attorney, who may answer even without personal knowledge; attorney answers may expose the entity to additional discovery and possible disqualification. Responses must be signed by the person making them and objections signed by the attorney making them.

rubrics_metrics.name: When requests for production may be served
rubrics_metrics.description: For inter partes proceedings commenced on or after November 1, 2007, discovery including requests for production may be served only during the discovery period and provided the serving party has either previously served or is serving concurrently its initial disclosures, absent stipulation or Board order to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for production may be served through the last day of the discovery period even though responses may be served after the discovery period closes. If combined with a deposition notice, production requests must be served at least 35 days before the deposition (if served by mail/Express/overnight courier) or at least 30 days before (if other methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for production cannot be served on nonparties
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for production may not be served on a non-party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a discovery deposition deponent is a nonparty witness in the U.S., production at the deposition may be obtained by subpoena duces tecum (Fed. R. Civ. P. 45); a subpoena is unnecessary if the witness voluntarily produces documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-country limitations and sanctions considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties seeking production from a natural person residing in a foreign country should be aware foreign laws may preclude such discovery; in determining sanctions for non-compliance due to conflict with foreign laws, the Board considers (1) good faith of non-complying party, (2) whether non-complying party would incur foreign criminal liability, (3) whether alternative sources are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Societe Internationale v. Rogers and subsequent case law when foreign-law conflicts arise; consider alternatives and good faith before seeking sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of production under Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(a) and Rule 26(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request production and inspection of designated documents, ESI, and tangible things in the responding party's possession, custody, or control, and may request entry onto land to inspect property, subject to the scope limits of Rule 26(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESI includes writings, drawings, graphs, charts, photographs, sound recordings, images, and other data stored in any medium from which information can be obtained. Entry on land requests are rarely used in Board proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation to locate documents not in possession/custody/control or to create documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A party generally does not have an obligation to locate documents that are not in its possession, custody or control and cannot be required to produce documents that do not exist or that it would have to create.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party may not mislead adversary by promising to produce documents and then failing to do so while claiming absence of possession/control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements required in a request for production (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must (A) describe with reasonable particularity each item or category of items to be inspected; (B) specify a reasonable time, place, and manner for inspection; and (C) may specify the form(s) in which ESI is to be produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are expected to discuss ESI production formats during the mandatory discovery conference (Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)); Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(1)(C) allows but does not require a requested format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and content of responses to requests for production (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The responding party must respond in writing within 30 days after being served. For each item/category, the response must either state inspection will be permitted as requested or state an objection including reasons. An objection to part of a request must specify the part and permit inspection of the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If objecting to ESI production form (or if no form specified), the responding party must state the form(s) it intends to use. For items not objected to, state whether responsive documents exist and whether they will be produced or withheld on privilege grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing documents and ESI — form and organization (Fed. R. Civ. P. 34(b)(2)(E))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless stipulated or ordered, a party must produce documents as they are kept in the ordinary course of business or must organize and label them to correspond to the categories in the request. If a request does not specify a form for producing ESI, a party must produce it in a form in which it is ordinarily maintained or in a reasonably usable form. A party need not produce the same ESI in more than one form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents produced in ESI not kept in the ordinary course must be organized and labeled to correspond to request categories. A responding party should not convert ESI into a form that makes it more difficult or burdensome for the requesting party to use. The Board may order place/manner/form of production on motion (37 CFR § 2.120(d)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Place and manner of production (37 CFR § 2.120(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Production of documents and things is made at the place where documents are usually kept, or where the parties agree, or where and in the manner the Board orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties often copy and forward produced documents at the requesting party’s expense as a courtesy and efficiency; parties should discuss production logistics in their discovery conference. The Board may order photocopying and mailing where appropriate as a sanction.
